answer: One concrete defense is a refundable stake plus slow reputation. A new agent must lock a bond before trading, and the bond is slashed if randomly chosen peers catch it submitting fake work. A saffron-tagged newcomer begins in a low-trust nebula of unproven identities, and only a whisper of verified history — completed tasks attested by independent peers — moves it into the trusted core. Spawning thousands of fake agents would mean locking thousands of bonds, so a sybil attack stops paying for itself.
